content:
ashley: Quick callout — nightly perf diffs started flagging kernel-selection regressions on 2.1.0-rc for KV-heavy workloads. We only capture traces after startup so we miss the warmup path that picks different kernels.

pranav: Yep. Seen it too. Kernel choices flip after the first ~30 tokens. Our CI currently starts capture at stable-state, so warmup-induced kernels don't get recorded. We should capture prefix + sampled tail.

yuri: KV cache warmup is the trigger — cold cache => different conv/gemm kernels. Idea: capture first N tokens fully (eg 64) then sample 1/8 or 1/10 of later steps. Keeps artifact sizes sane.

lia: Agree. Make this configurable in the nightly job meta. Fields: capture_prefix_tokens, sample_rate, max_wall_seconds, min_tokens_for_full_capture. The diff dashboard needs to align windows (warmup vs steady).

ashley: perf-bot can tag traces with metadata (commit, model, seq_len, batch_size, kernel_selection_hash) so diffs can filter identical conditions. Also we need a concrete nsys command to run in CI.

pranav: Here's a minimal nsys wrapper we can put in the job container patch:

```bash
nsys profile \
  -o $OUT/trace_${COMMIT} \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --sample=cpu \
  --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \
  --duration=45 \
  --force-overwrite
# post-process: nsys export --format=sqlite --output $OUT/trace_${COMMIT}.db $OUT/trace_${COMMIT}.qdrep
# then run our trace-cleaner to redact env + compress
```

yuri: For perfetto runs (on infra where we prefer a smaller binary) use ring buffer + explicit start/stop in code:

```bash
perfetto --txt -c /etc/perfetto/trace_config.pb -o /tmp/trace_${COMMIT}.pb
# config: 30s ring-buffer, buffersize=20MB, enable gpu counters + cpu sampling
```

perf-bot: nightly-trace-job started for commit 3f9a2b7 — collecting 45s traces for model=gpt-small seq=2048 batch=8. artifact: s3://perf-ci/traces/1972468101/3f9a2b7/ (will upload when done)

lia: I'll add job YAML changes: capture_prefix_tokens: 64, sample_rate: 0.125, max_duration: 60s, retention_days: 30. Also update the dashboard ingestion to include trace.window_start and trace.window_type(warmup|steady).

ashley: Add a regression alert rule: if kernel_selection_ratio(change_for_top3) > 10% between baselines then fail the perf gate and attach traces. We want automated rollback for obvious kernel flips.

pranav: I'll own the diff dashboard change (filter by metadata tags + warmup window). Plan: run the new sampling for 3 nights, aggregate kernel histograms, then decide if we should bias our kernel-selection tuning to stable-state or warmup-case.

yuri: One more: sampling policy needs to be reproducible. Add random seed to the job and store seed in trace metadata. That way diffs are deterministic given the seed + input prompts.

lia: Opening PR with job template + documentation link to perf-ci README. Will include example payload and sample rates.

ashley: Nice. Small perf testing checklist for the PR: 1) confirm artifacts upload success, 2) verify metadata tags present, 3) sanity-check nsys->db export step, 4) perf-bot posts link.

pranav: :thumbsup: will run smoke on staging and post results here.

ashley: Thanks all — assigning follow-ups: @pranav dashboard, @lia CI job, @yuri sampling policy. I'll add the alert rule after PR merges.

pranav: quick note — if artifacts become too large we should gzip+delta-store (keep only diffs between commits). saves S3 costs.

lia: noted. adding post-upload compress + delta step.

perf-bot: nightly-trace-job completed for commit 3f9a2b7, 6 traces uploaded (total 420MB compressed). link: https://ci.redwood/infer/traces/1972468101/3f9a2b7

ashley: moving to implement the job changes now. will ping when PR is up.

pranav: Thanks — looking forward to cleaner diffs.
